- Overestimate prices when sentiment is negative or volatile (especially after recent spikes), especially in early forecast windows.  
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative or shows strong downward momentum.  
- Overshoot after sharp upward sentiment spikes; reduce forecast peak by 5–15% in subsequent periods.  
- Mean-revert forecasts when sentiment shows prolonged negative drift or low volatility.  
- Avoid overconfidence in early forecast windows; adjust downward if sentiment history shows strong downward bias.  
- Lagged sentiment (e.g., 3–5 day average) should be used to dampen overreaction in short-term forecasts.
